metadata.subject: Physics
metadata.note: 2m: define half-life. Cloze: 'time(0.5m) / activity or number of radioactive nuclei(1m) / half(0.5m)'. Key discriminator: students must specify WHAT halves (activity OR number of nuclei) — just saying 'time to halve' earns 0m.

question.name: CSEC Phy May 2022 Q1b(i) — Define Half-Life
question.text:
Define the term 'half-life' by completing the statement below:

Half-life is the [[1]] taken for the [[2]] of a radioactive sample to decrease to [[3]] of its initial value.
question.general_feedback:
Half-life (t½):

Half-life is the time taken for the activity (or the number of radioactive nuclei) of a radioactive sample to decrease to half its initial value.

Note: The activity (disintegrations per second) and the number of undecayed nuclei both halve in one half-life — either is acceptable in the definition.

Example: If a sample has activity 800 Bq and t½ = 2 hours, after 2 hours activity = 400 Bq; after 4 hours = 200 Bq, and so on.

ddwtos.cloze_html: Half-life is the [[1]] taken for the [[2]] of a radioactive sample to decrease to [[3]] of its initial value.

groups.label: Half-life is the ___ taken for...
groups.diagnostic_hint: Half-life is a TIME (measured in seconds, minutes, years, etc.). It measures duration, not energy or temperature.

groups.label: Half-life — ___ to fall to half
groups.diagnostic_hint: The ACTIVITY (or number of radioactive nuclei, or count rate) falls to HALF its original value in one half-life. "Mass" is sometimes accepted but activity/count rate is more precise.

groups.label: Half-life — falls to ___ its original value
groups.diagnostic_hint: After one half-life, exactly HALF the original activity remains. After two half-lives, one-quarter remains. After n half-lives: (½)ⁿ of the original activity remains.

ddwtos.word_bank_note: 12 tokens for 3 slots. Slot 1 (time): 'energy' and 'temperature' are unrelated to the definition of half-life. 'rate' is tempting since activity is a rate, but the question asks for what is TAKEN (time). Slot 2 (activity/number of nuclei): both correct — CSEC accepts either. 'mass' is a critical distractor: mass does halve eventually (as nuclei decay to stable daughters), but CSEC mark schemes require 'activity' or 'number of (radioactive) nuclei'. 'radiation dose' is vague and refers to absorbed/received dose, not sample property. Slot 3 (half): 'one quarter' is what you get after TWO half-lives — common off-by-one error. 'one tenth' has no special significance. 'zero' is incorrect — radioactivity never reaches exactly zero in finite time (exponential decay).
